```{r}
model <- readRDS("../results/multiclass-model.rds")
percent <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * x)
binary_all <- readRDS("../results/binary_final_comparison.rds")
binary_results <- binary_all[binary_all$variant == "2. more epochs + early stopping", ]
binary_baseline <- binary_all[binary_all$variant == "1. baseline (25 units, dropout 0.2, 5 epochs)", ]
```

### Abstract

We developed binary and five-category models from webpage text. Both models improved on their baselines and generated predictions for all 929 test pages.

### Preprocessing

**Part (a):** Paragraph text was cleaned and converted into TF-IDF word-importance scores.

**Part (b):** Titles, headings, and paragraphs were cleaned and converted into TF-IDF scores for words and word pairs.

### Methods

**Part (a):** We compared neural networks, SVM, and regularized logistic regression. The selected network used early stopping. The final network used 90% of cleaned labeled pages for fitting and 10% for early stopping.

**Part (b):** We tuned ridge multinomial regression and evaluated it on a separate validation set, keeping pages from the same subject together. The final model used all 2,165 labeled pages.

### Results

```{r}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Model = c("(a) Neural network", "(b) Ridge multinomial regression"),
  Accuracy = percent(c(binary_results$accuracy, model$metrics$Accuracy)),
  Sensitivity = percent(c(binary_results$sensitivity, model$metrics$Sensitivity)),
  Specificity = percent(c(binary_results$specificity, model$metrics$Specificity))))
```

Part (b)'s sensitivity and specificity give equal weight to all five classes.

### Comparison of models and results

**Part (a):** Early stopping increased accuracy from `r percent(binary_baseline$accuracy)` to `r percent(binary_results$accuracy)`, the highest recorded accuracy among the binary alternatives. These comparisons informed model selection, so this is a development estimate.

**Part (b):** Accuracy was `r percent(model$metrics$Accuracy)`, compared with `r percent(model$baseline_accuracy)` for always predicting the most common class. Fewer than half of “Physical Activity” and “Other claim content” pages were correctly identified.

**Overall:** Both models improved on their own baselines and produced the required test predictions. Their accuracies do not directly rank the methods because the tasks and validation splits differ. Improving recognition of the weaker multiclass categories remains a priority.
